_comment: Kernel-purity gate policy (DATA, not code). ADR-0547 / FRIC-1781129000(b). A crate named *-kernel or *-core is the clean-architecture cutover-stable seam (its interfaces must not change when ADR-0510 transient infrastructure is replaced at owned-stack cutover). This gate asserts no such crate — nor any workspace-internal crate reachable through its path-dependency closure — directly depends on a denylisted transient-tech crate, unless an explicit reasoned exception is declared below. ALL repo-specifics are DATA here: a different repo adopts the gate by repointing kernel_crate_globs / deny / min_expected_kernel_crates; the Rust engine hardcodes no oyatie crate name. The denylist targets TRANSIENT INFRA ADAPTERS (kube, sqlx, rustls, the AWS SDKs, etcd) that get discarded at cutover — NOT legitimate cutover-stable kernel primitives (aws-lc-rs, libc, zeroize, tokio), which are deliberately absent from the deny set so they never false-positive. The kube/kuberos trap: `kube` is exact + `kube-` is a HYPHEN-bounded prefix so the kube-* family is denied without matching the owned kuberos/oya-cloud-kernel-* crates; the same hyphen discipline keeps `aws-sdk-` from ever matching the primitive aws-lc-rs.

deny.reason: transient k8s client (cloud-k8s owned at cutover)
transient TLS adapter (owned transport at cutover)
transient SQL adapter (cloud-data owned at cutover)
transient AWS SDK adapters (owned cloud services at cutover)
transient etcd adapter (owned quorum substrate at cutover)

transient external IdP client adapter (cloud-iam IS the IdP substrate per founder directive 2026-06-10; oya/identity consumes cloud IdP, not a parallel IdP; zitadel is a transient adapter not the W5 destination)
zitadel satellite crates — same transient-adapter rationale as the exact zitadel entry

_undenied_http_stack_rationale: axum, reqwest, tonic, and hyper are deliberately absent from the deny set. They are cutover-stable HTTP/gRPC primitives whose wire interfaces are not expected to change at ADR-0510 owned-stack cutover — the owned transport layer presents the same hyper/tonic surface. Denying them would produce false positives on legitimate kernel crates that own their HTTP/gRPC port definitions. hyper-rustls IS denied (above) because it couples hyper with the transient rustls TLS adapter specifically. If a future owned-stack replacement changes this assessment, add the relevant crate here with a cutover reference.

product_contract.born_blocking: All kernel/core crates are pure today, so the expected finding set is empty and the gate is RED-blocking on arrival: a NEW kernel-with-transient-dep (directly or via its workspace-internal path-dep closure) fails closed immediately. No shrink-only legacy baseline is needed.
product_contract.pack_shaped: kernel_crate_globs, deny, exceptions, and min_expected_kernel_crates are DATA; the Rust kernel hardcodes no oyatie crate name. A different repo adopts the gate by repointing this policy.
product_contract.closure_rule: For each glob-matched kernel, the gate walks the workspace-internal dependency closure (Cargo path deps + local BUCK deps) and applies the deny set to every reached node's direct external deps in [dependencies]/[build-dependencies]/[target.*.dependencies] (dev-dependencies excluded). This closes the escape where a kernel pulls a transient crate through a local adapter path-dep while staying directly clean.
product_contract.primitive_safety: Legitimate cutover-stable kernel primitives (aws-lc-rs, libc, zeroize, tokio) are absent from the deny set, so they never false-positive; the kube exact + kube- hyphen-prefix shape denies the kube-* family without matching the owned kuberos/oya-cloud-kernel-* crates.
product_contract.coverage_scope: The gate scans the ROOT workspace members only. The 4 oya-cloud-kernel-{frame,hal,ksync,user-layout}-kernel crates live in the cloud/cloud-kernel nested no_std workspace, listed under root [workspace].exclude, and are structurally outside the scan (bare-metal no_std; transient infra deps implausible). 2026-08-20: deleting 45 zero-importer libs/ crates removed ~30 *-kernel-named crates from the count outright (their gate logic is gone, not moved); the scanned census drops 156 -> 126 kernel/core crates and min_expected_kernel_crates follows it down to 126. Scanning nested workspaces is a reserved v2 extension.
product_contract.known_limitations: v1 reads declared deps from Cargo.toml [dependencies]/[build-dependencies]/[target.*.dependencies]/[target.*.build-dependencies] (dev-deps excluded) + BUCK rust_library deps; member-level `package = "<real>"` renames are denied on the real name; build.rs is scanned for build-dep liveness and build-deps are never auto-fixed. NOT yet resolved: (a) a `dep = { workspace = true }` whose root [workspace.dependencies] entry uses `package =` or `path =` (latent deliberate-evasion route; root manifest has zero such renames today); (b) a BUCK-only kernel crate (BUCK but no Cargo.toml, like the sanctioned oya-cloud-ci-rust-first-automation-hygiene-app) is not enumerated by the Cargo-workspace-member resolver, so a future BUCK-only *-kernel crate is unscanned (no such crate exists today). Full feature-resolved transitive closure is reserved as KP-TRANSIENT-DEP-TRANSITIVE. The threat model is accidental seam mis-draws; a deliberate evader could equally edit this policy.

purpose: Kernel-purity dependency gate. *-kernel/*-core crates are the clean-arch cutover-stable seam; they (and their workspace-internal closure) must carry zero ADR-0510 transient-tech dependencies. Makes the FRIC-1781129000 port/adapter seam-mis-draw class impossible to ship.
